opcode.name: OP_GuildList
opcode.comment: [ffff — needs re-hunt] GuildListCode. The prior note claiming a 14176b login packet held guild names is WRONG: 2026-07-28 content-dumped that packet and its 81 strings are housing plot addresses (street name + plot number), i.e. a neighborhood/housing list, not guilds. No guild-name list was seen anywhere in the world stream of a 3-login capture — a full server guild roster may no longer ride the world stream at login. Re-hunt against a capture that opens the guild window.

opcode.name: OP_MOTD
opcode.comment: [ffff — needs re-hunt] MOTDCode, server message of the day. NOT FOUND on 2026-07-28: no readable-text S>C packet appeared post-OP_EnterWorld in a 3-login world capture. Prior fingerprint was a ~154b readable-text payload. May now ride the zone stream (see the OP_MOTD zone-vs-world note) or fire only when the MOTD changes.

opcode.name: OP_SendLoginInfo
opcode.comment: Client starting world session by asking for login information. Live: 464b C>S, the FIRST packet of every world session. Re-confirmed 2026-07-28 on a 3-login Live world capture (3/3 sessions, always packet #1). Zero competing unknowns at 464b C>S.

opcode.name: OP_LogServer
opcode.comment: [ffff — unresolved, two candidates] Live world handshake. Candidate A: a 24b S>C packet that fires immediately after OP_SendLoginInfo in all 3 logins (position matches the historical fingerprint, but 24b is too small to carry the classic server-info block and the payload is opaque). Candidate B: a 1984b S>C packet later in the same burst whose only string is the world shortname. Legacy 6.4.25 defines no logServerStruct, so there is no struct to size-check against and neither candidate could be confirmed 2026-07-28. Resolve with a capture on a DIFFERENT world server — the payload carrying the changed shortname is OP_LogServer.

opcode.name: OP_ApproveWorld
opcode.comment: [ffff — needs re-hunt] Small S>C in the handshake band; still not isolated. 2026-07-28: several small S>C packets (0b, 12b, 16b, 72b, 92b) fire in the band with no distinguishing content; needs a capture of a REJECTED world entry (full server / locked) to contrast against a successful one.

opcode.name: OP_EnterWorld
opcode.comment: Client tells world server to enter world with selected char. Live: 72b C>S, char name (zero-padded) at offset 0, 64b of zeros, 0xffffffff trailer at offset 68. Server REUSES the same id for two shorter S>C variants (1b ack, 7b name echo) — all three observed. Re-confirmed 2026-07-28 (3/3 logins); byte layout matched the recorded fingerprint exactly.

opcode.name: OP_ExpansionInfo
opcode.comment: Which expansions user has. Live: 64b fixed S>C in the handshake band. Re-confirmed 2026-07-28 (3/3 logins) — it is the ONLY 64b S>C opcode in the world stream, so zero competitors at that size+direction. NOTE evidence class: size + direction + handshake position + zero-competitor. The payload is opaque (no strings, no obvious bitmask), so the field layout is NOT confirmed; treat as identification-only until a capture with a changed expansion set is diffed.

opcode.name: OP_SendCharInfo
opcode.comment: [ffff — needs re-hunt] Send all chars visible @ char select. NOT FOUND on 2026-07-28: every S>C world payload in a 3-login capture was content-scanned for the logged-in character name and only the chatserver tuple and OP_EnterWorld carried it. The two large early S>C packets were ruled out — one is a housing plot list, the other a 36873b binary table whose only string is a timezone id. The prior note claiming 14176b was a mis-attribution of the same packet as OP_GuildList.

opcode.name: OP_SendSpellChecksum
opcode.comment: Contains a snippet of spell data. Live: 2056b C>S, position 2 of 4 in the post-handshake checksum burst. Content-confirmed 2026-07-28: payload tail is caret-delimited text in spells_us.txt record format (integer fields only).

opcode.name: OP_SendExeChecksum
opcode.comment: Client-side eqgame.exe checksum sample. Live: 2056b C>S, position 1 of 4 in the post-handshake checksum burst. Content-confirmed 2026-07-28: payload tail is x86-64 machine code (recognisable mov/test/je sequences), unlike the caret-delimited text of the other 2056b members.

opcode.name: OP_SendBaseDataChecksum
opcode.comment: Client-side base-data file sample. Live: 2056b C>S, position 3 of 4 in the post-handshake checksum burst. Content-confirmed 2026-07-28: payload tail is caret-delimited text carrying DECIMAL/float fields (per-level stat tables) — that float content is what separates it from the integer-only spell records at position 2.

opcode.name: OP_SendSkillCapsChecksum
opcode.comment: Client-side skillcaps checksum. Live: 64b C>S, opaque hash-style payload, position 4 of 4 in the checksum burst and the only member not at 2056b. Re-confirmed 2026-07-28 (3/3 logins); zero competing unknowns at 64b C>S.

opcode.name: OP_SetChatServer
opcode.comment: Legacy chatserver tuple — NOT obsolete on Live (the prior 'may be obsolete' note is disproven). Live: 62b S>C, ASCII comma-delimited tuple: chat-host,port,worldshortname.charname,ticket,flag. Fires immediately before OP_ZoneServerInfo on each world->zone handoff. Content-confirmed 2026-07-28; the embedded port matches WorldServerChat2Port and the observed chat session. Payload carries identity + a session ticket — never quote literal bytes.

opcode.name: OP_SetChatServer2
opcode.comment: Secondary chat / account / commerce service catalog. Live: 1464b S>C in the handshake band, ~18 plaintext Daybreak service URLs (auth/account/wallet endpoints). Content-confirmed 2026-07-28 (3/3 logins) — payload opens with a length-prefixed URL list.

opcode.name: OP_ZoneServerInfo
opcode.comment: Zone server connection info. Live: 130b S>C, fires on world->zone handoff. zoneServerInfoStruct is UNCHANGED across the 07/15 rotation — char ip[128] holds a NUL-terminated 'eqzone-NN.everquest.com' hostname (tail is uninitialised client stack, ignore it), uint16 port at offset 128. Confirmed 2026-07-28 against a Live world+zone capture: the 130b S>C world payload's trailing port matched the port of the zone session the client opened moments later. PRIORITY 10 — the daemon binds a box's zone stream off this opcode; while it is unmapped no zone session ever binds, and with >1 box on the wire (any client that has zoned once) BoxRegistry drops every unbound zone packet, so the whole zone stream decodes to nothing. Re-hunt this FIRST after every patch. Legacy's 777c is stale (dated 2012) and matched nothing on the current wire.

opcode.name: OP_WorldComplete
opcode.comment: Client telling world server it is done. Live: 0b C>S, the LAST C>S packet of the session, fires immediately after OP_ZoneServerInfo; world then disconnects. Re-confirmed 2026-07-28 on both world->zone handoffs in a 3-login capture (2/2).

opcode.name: OP_DeleteCharacter
opcode.comment: Delete character @ char select. Live: 68b C>S world, name@offset 0. Re-confirmed post-2026-05-22 patch (login-charmgmt): 1 C>S fire carrying the deleted char name.

opcode.name: OP_CharacterCreate
opcode.comment: Create character @ char select. Live: 168b C>S world (name[64] + gender/race/class/deity/appearance fields), fires once per submitted creation right after OP_ApproveName response. Re-confirmed post-2026-05-22 patch (login-charmgmt).

opcode.name: OP_ApproveName
opcode.comment: Approving new character name @ char creation. Live: 84b C>S name candidate, 1b S>C status (taken vs available). Re-confirmed post-2026-05-22 patch (login-charmgmt): fires right before OP_CharacterCreate.

opcode.name: OP_RandomNameGenerator
opcode.comment: Returns a random name. May be obsolete on Live — repeated random-button presses during char creation produced no isolated wire request/response; names likely come pre-baked in char-select catalog dump.
